idea: Themed weeks, School and health day: a replacement written after the first script for this slot was held; written from the source, then corrected by an independent editor before voicing.
description: In Jharkhand, 38.7% of mothers with a recent birth had four or more pregnancy check-ups (antenatal care visits) in the 2019-21 family health survey, and 59.0% in the 2023-24 survey: up 20.3 points, about three times India's rise of 6.7 points (58.5% to 65.2%).

Against India's figure, Jharkhand went from about two-thirds to about nine-tenths. Survey estimates: small gaps are not differences, and small states and territories swing more. The survey shows how many, not why.
source: International Institute for Population Sciences, National Family Health Survey: NFHS-6 (2023-24) state fact sheets, which also print the NFHS-5 (2019-21) figure. Mothers with 4+ antenatal care visits (pregnancy check-ups) for a recent birth. 34 states and UTs with a figure in both surveys; Lakshadweep (small sample) is not ranked and Manipur has no figure in the sheets used. Survey estimates.
